archetype.name: Playoff Team (pass-driven offense)
archetype.definition: A team whose top-five passing attack does most of the work while a middling defense, poor discipline and shaky special teams keep the margins thinner than its efficiency suggests.

report.headline: Jackson's arm is carrying a 3-1 team whose defense and discipline lag behind.
report.take:
Under first-year coach Jesse Minter, Baltimore is a passing team that thinks it is a running team. Derrick Henry has 89 carries, about 22 a game, and the Ravens run more than the situation calls for (pass rate over expected 25th). The efficiency, though, lives through the air. Their 0.328 EPA per dropback ranks 2nd, and their 50.2% offensive success rate also ranks 2nd. The run game piles up yardage, 153.5 a game, but its EPA is slightly negative, and it went into the red in each of the last two weeks. This isn't new: the offense ranked 1st in EPA in 2024, so the passing efficiency has a real track record behind it.

The caveat is who they've thrown on. The four defenses Baltimore has faced now rank 22nd, 30th, 31st and 21st. The worst offensive day came against one of them: 17 points in a home loss to New Orleans as an 8.5-point favorite. A 0.328 pass EPA built against that slate will come down. The question is how far once Cleveland, Cincinnati and Jacksonville show up.

The record is honest, if not quite as strong as the efficiency. Wins over expected are only +0.19, and the +0.8 turnover margin is helping but isn't propping anything up. What drags the point differential (+5 a game) below a 5th-ranked net EPA is self-inflicted. They average 9.8 penalties a game (30th), including 5 on the line alone (29th), with 131 penalty yards against Tennessee. Special teams cost 1.8 EPA a game (25th). They convert only 22.2% in short yardage (31st) while going for it on every fourth down they can. That combination also explains a 1-2-1 cover record: they win, but they leave points on the field.

The defense is average, with a split personality. Underneath it's stingy: short-pass EPA allowed ranks 4th and overall pass EPA 9th. But it can't stop the run (27th in rush EPA allowed) and barely pressures the quarterback (14.7%, 27th). Now Trey Hendrickson is out with a fractured finger and Marlon Humphrey is questionable. Add a questionable Jackson ankle and two interior linemen on IR, and this is the first real test of the depth behind the starters.

strengths.title: Elite dropback efficiency
strengths.body: Baltimore is 2nd in pass EPA per play and 2nd in success rate. Passing EPA has topped 10 in three of four games, including 12.0 against Tennessee. Jackson's history (1st-ranked offense in 2024 and 2019) says much of this is real. The soft defensive slate says the exact number won't hold.

strengths.title: Clean pockets despite long holds
strengths.body: Jackson holds the ball 3.1 seconds on average (2nd-longest), yet the line has allowed only 13 QB hits (3rd fewest) and a 10th-ranked pressure rate. That patience feeds the downfield passing game. It's the strength most exposed by the losses of guard Jovaughn Gwyn and center Ethan Pocic.

strengths.title: Tight coverage underneath
strengths.body: The secondary takes away the short game, ranking 4th in EPA allowed on short passes. That keeps the overall pass defense 9th even without a rush. It is coverage-driven, so Humphrey's calf matters more than usual.

concerns.title: Jackson's ankle and a thinning line
concerns.body: Jackson is questionable, and his coach said he doesn't know the chances yet. Tyler Huntley is the fallback and has thrown for 63 yards in his one appearance. The interior line has already lost Gwyn (91% of snaps) and Pocic to IR, and Ronnie Stanley and Andrew Vorhees are questionable. The offense's whole identity rests on Jackson having time.

concerns.title: No pass rush, soft run defense
concerns.body: A 14.7% pressure rate (27th) and 27th-ranked rush EPA allowed form a real structural flaw, not a role cost. Dallas ran for 148 yards on them. Losing Hendrickson makes the rush thinner still. Opponents with a functional ground game can stay on schedule all day.

concerns.title: Penalties, special teams, short yardage
concerns.body: The Ravens average 9.8 penalties a game (30th), lose 1.8 EPA a game on special teams (25th) and convert just 22.2% in short yardage (31st). That is the gap between a 5th-ranked net EPA and a modest +5 point differential. Penalty rates can be coached down, but a new staff hasn't shown it yet.

trend.note: Passing has been consistently strong apart from the Week 2 dud against New Orleans, posting 10+ EPA in the other three games. The run game has gone the other way, from +6.7 rushing EPA in Week 1 to negative totals in Weeks 3 and 4.

nextGame.headline: Everything hinges on Jackson's ankle against Atlanta's wall-like run defense
nextGame.body:
Atlanta is built to take away what Baltimore leans on. The Falcons rank 1st in rush EPA allowed and 1st in explosive run rate allowed, so Henry-heavy early downs are likely to stall. Their 26.5% pressure rate (4th) meets a quarterback who holds the ball 3.1 seconds behind a patched interior line. The opening is the secondary, which is merely 10th-11th in pass defense. Baltimore's path is to throw more than usual. Atlanta's offense is a mirror image: 2nd in rush EPA and 2nd in rush success, but 31st in pass EPA after starting three different quarterbacks. That ground game points straight at Baltimore's weakest unit, and Penix's 2.45-second release (fastest in the league) blunts a pass rush that barely exists anyway.

Availability decides this one. If Jackson plays, the Ravens hold a clear edge in overall quality and face a team that has turned it over 2 more times than its opponents per game. If it's Huntley, Baltimore's passing advantage shrinks sharply. Then a 2.5-point spread looks optimistic against a top-eight defense. Hendrickson and Chris Moore are out, and Humphrey, Stanley and Smythe are questionable. On Atlanta's side, left tackle Jake Matthews (100% snaps) and edge Za'Darius Smith are questionable after leaving Monday's game.

keyMatchups.title: Henry versus the league's best run defense
keyMatchups.body: Baltimore averages 153.5 rushing yards a game but has been negative in rush EPA lately. Atlanta allows -0.307 EPA per rush and almost no explosive runs. Without Gwyn and Pocic inside, the Ravens should expect a long day of short gains and have to win through the air.

keyMatchups.title: Atlanta's pressure against long dropbacks
keyMatchups.body: Atlanta's 4th-ranked pressure rate tests Baltimore's 3.1-second average hold time and a reshuffled interior line. With Jackson, extended plays have been an asset. A limited Jackson or Huntley turns them into sacks.

keyMatchups.title: Falcons' run game into Baltimore's soft spot
keyMatchups.body: Atlanta's offense only works on the ground: 2nd in rush EPA and 2nd in yards per carry, against 31st in pass EPA. Baltimore ranks 27th against the run. If the Falcons stay on schedule, they can control the clock and shorten the game.

nextGame.watch: Whether Jackson is active, and whether Baltimore abandons the Henry-first script early to attack Atlanta's secondary.

restOfSeason.body:
The passing efficiency is the most durable thing here; Jackson has run league-best offenses before. Still, a 0.328 pass EPA built against four bottom-third defenses will slide toward the merely very good once Cleveland, Cincinnati and Jacksonville arrive in the next five weeks. The defense looks like what it was in 2025: around the middle, good in coverage, bad against the run. The pass rush gets no help while Hendrickson is out. The penalties and special-teams leaks are the most fixable problems, and the likeliest source of upside if Minter's staff cleans them up.

The schedule is back-loaded with six division games against three rivals all within one game of first place. That makes the AFC North a four-team race, not a coronation. The middle stretch includes 0-4 Chargers, Texans and Bucs teams. LAC and TB both have defenses ranked 11th and 5th, though, so those won't be easy points. With a healthy Jackson this is a 10-to-12 win team. A multi-week absence knocks a win or two off that quickly.
swingFactors: Jackson's ankle and how many games he misses
Interior line health with Gwyn and Pocic on IR
Whether the penalty rate comes down under the new staff

bets.reason: Both teams run more than expected (Baltimore -5.1, Atlanta -10 pass rate over expected) and rank top-10 in time of possession, which shortens the game. Atlanta's #1 run defense should stall Henry, and the Falcons' 31st-ranked passing offense averages 17 points. The uncertainty over Jackson pushes the same way.

bets.lean: BAL -2.5 (only if Jackson is confirmed active)
bets.reason: With Jackson, the net EPA gap is wide (0.152 vs. -0.1), and Atlanta is last in turnover margin at -2 per game. The number likely reflects his questionable tag. Without him, pass, because the Ravens are 1-2-1 ATS even at full strength.
Atlanta allows -0.307 EPA per rush and the fewest explosive runs in the league. Baltimore's rushing EPA has been negative two weeks running, and the interior line has lost two players to IR.

confidence.note: Four games against weak defenses, a new coach, and Jackson's status unresolved.
